name: _Organized Desktop/05 Numbered Experiments/j4

summary: Excellent durable-CRUD engine (unique identity, advisory sidecar lock, stale-bytes optimistic check, atomic Files.move, publish-after-commit) with 28 behavioral tests that all exist on disk and an unusually candid VERIFICATION.md. Every spot-checked claim (menu 4/5/6, 2-26 choice range, duplicate-ID rejection, --release 17 -Xlint:all) matched the code. Blocked from the learning path by stack: pure Java CLI, web/SQL left entirely as prose exercises; run.ps1 is Windows-only and lacks the JAVA_HOME fallback its siblings have.

name: _Organized Desktop/05 Numbered Experiments/j5
top_fix: Add a TypeScript/Express + SQLite port of ExpenseManager.updateExpense and ExpenseFileStorage.save (Zod validation, 400/404/409/204, transaction in place of the atomic move); also ship the data/ fixture the docs promise but that does not exist.
summary: The best teaching artifact of the three Java experiments: Astra found a real data-loss bug (blank optional note vanishing on reload), wrote the failing test first, then hardened load/save so malformed files fail loudly rather than dropping records. Validate-then-serialize-then-ATOMIC_MOVE is shown with the invariant in a comment, exercises and solutions are properly separated, and the practice ladder attacks a limitation of Astra's own code (nextId reuse after deleting the newest record) that VERIFICATION.md also admits. 23 claimed tests = 23 on disk. Off-stack, and astraupskill/README.md references a data/ directory that is not in the project.

name: _Organized Desktop/05 Numbered Experiments/j7
top_fix: Add 08-THE-SAME-ORDER-IN-CSHARP.md rendering Order/OrderItem/OrderStatus as EF Core entities with an owned line-item price snapshot, showing how Include(o => o.Items) reproduces the exact restoration bug that was fixed.
summary: The richest domain model of the three Java experiments and the closest to real .NET/EF Core work. Astra found an aggregate-restoration bug (order rebuilt discount-before-items, so every saved discount was silently clamped to zero on reload), fixed it by restoring the whole aggregate at once, then added detached reads, PAID-rejects-edits, sub-cent rejection and one versioned atomic snapshot replacing four independent entity files. 35 claimed tests = 35 on disk; VERIFICATION.md distinguishes automated from source-reviewed coverage. Off-stack, no C#/TS rendering, and the promised data/ fixture directory does not exist so the walkthrough starts with manual data entry.

name: _Organized Desktop/08 App And Product Projects/job track/live-chat-support-platform
top_fix: Move the mark_read range query inside the transaction (server/src/socket.js:132-139) - the read-then-write TOCTOU the course teaches against still exists in the same file - and write it up as a seventh defect.
summary: Strongest on-stack artifact in B17. Six live-state defects reproduced by tests that failed against the old code (6/6, corroborated by the delivery JSON) then fixed: per-user socket-set presence, one bound identity per connection, insert+room-update+receipt in one db.transaction with broadcast strictly after commit, and rowid tie-breaking so equal timestamps do not over-mark receipts. Failure injection uses a real SQLite ABORT trigger. Docs and evidence agree that no browser test was run. Windows-only npm.cmd commands, UTF-8 BOM on all 9 files, and one unmentioned read-then-write race in mark_read.

name: _Organized Desktop/08 App And Product Projects/job track/restaurant-kitchen-display-system
top_fix: Turn the disclosed limit into the course's best exercise: document the existence check that sits outside the transaction (server/src/routes/api.js:192-197), have the learner write the interleaving that makes the 404 stale, then implement updated_at compare-and-set.
summary: The best all-round CRUD course in the batch. Real Express + SQLite + React where one action touches several rows and several screens. Four instructive fixes: ?includeLateOnly=false behaving like true, an order reporting ready while items were still queued, mutations committing while their audit row failed, and notifications emitted before commit. Each is pinned by a test that aborts an audit insert with a SQLite trigger and then asserts the database snapshot is unchanged. 12 claimed = 12 on disk with a retained TAP log; the 8-of-11 initial failure baseline and the 'no live browser' scope are both stated. Windows-only commands, BOM on all 9 files.

name: _Organized Desktop/08 App And Product Projects/job track/task-queue-system
top_fix: Make the Redis half runnable: add a docker-compose.yml (redis:7-alpine), an npm run redis:up script, and a 'no Docker on Windows' paragraph (WSL2 / Memurai) - roughly a third of the course is currently unexecutable as written.
summary: The most advanced course in B17 and the best statement of the dual-write problem. The original code ran DELETE FROM campaigns in its catch block, destroying work already accepted with a 201 when the broker was unreachable; a validation helper also returned the truthy Express response after a 400 so callers never short-circuited. Both are diffable against the backup. The replacement is a textbook transactional outbox: job ID persisted before the enqueue so a lost ack re-enqueues the same logical job, post-enqueue promotion guarded by WHERE status='pending', overlapping ticks blocked, dead-letter and requeue on the same pattern. 19 claimed = 19 on disk with a TAP log. Redis and Docker were unavailable so BullMQ execution was never run, which the README itself says; only 2 of the 19 tests are true pre-fix regressions.

name: _Organized Desktop/12 Other Projects/andie
top_fix: Reformat scripts/lib/*.js and test/migration.test.js to one statement per line with Prettier defaults (42 tests currently occupy 68 lines); nothing else matters for a junior until the code is readable - this alone moves D7 from 2 to 4.
summary: Genuine security find plus sharp integration engineering: the original script hard-coded live shpat_ admin tokens and ran a migration the moment you executed it. Astra replaced it with an offline-first plan/export/apply CLI where the plan is a reviewable artifact, conflicts surface instead of overwriting, cursors are passed as GraphQL variables and checked for advancement, reads retry with a bound while mutations never retry because an unacknowledged write has an unknown outcome. 42 claimed = 42 on disk, zero dependencies, engines pinned, no account needed - the easiest project in the batch to run. Held back by near-unreadable one-liner code style, error messages that discard userErrors detail entirely, and a domain that is API integration rather than CRUD web dev.

name: astra2
top_fix: Add 08-THE-SAME-REPOSITORY-BEHIND-AN-API.md: port voyages.ts to an Express/Next route handler over SQL with GET /voyages?q=&page=, PATCH with If-Match: <revision>, and map the existing VoyageError codes (conflict/invalid/missing/storage) to 409/400/404/500 - the abstraction is already right, only the transport is missing.
summary: A game project hiding one of the cleanest small CRUD systems in the review set: create/search/paginate, metadata edit, snapshot replacement, archive/restore, confirmed delete and export over IndexedDB, all guarded by an expected-revision token so a second tab cannot silently overwrite the first, with typed error codes that map directly onto HTTP status. Also fixes a real accounting bug (demolishing while a paused warehouse left the island over capacity applied a negative refund and consumed 600 wood), proved by a recorded original-vs-current measurement. The most trustworthy verification in the batch: real Chrome 152, hashed build assets proving the browser evidence came from a clean install, a self-reported sub-30-FPS late-game result, and an explicit refusal to inflate the 76-case count. No server, no SQL, no React; UI is innerHTML string assembly with a hand-rolled escape.
